text:
jess (Support): Alice from Acme reports embeddings mismatch between Hosted and Dedicated. Hosted returns 1536-d vectors, Dedicated endpoints return 768-d for the same text. Customer sees model alias 'redwood-embed-1' in both calls. They've also observed slower throughput and occasional 429s on Dedicated. Escalating for triage.

alice (Acme Inc.): repro steps: curl to hosted vs dedicated, same prompt, see different lengths. pasted curl and a short output below. Happy to provide logs. This started after we switched some traffic to dedicated last week.

alice (Acme Inc.): curl hosted:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\\   -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \\\   -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\\   -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-1", "input":"Acme product search"}'
```
response: {"data":[{"embedding":[<1536 floats>],"model":"redwood-embed-1","usage":{}}]}

alice (Acme Inc.): curl dedicated:
```
curl -X POST https://dedicated.acme.redwood/v1/embeddings \\\   -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACME_KEY" \\\   -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\\   -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-1", "input":"Acme product search"}'
```
response: {"data":[{"embedding":[<768 floats>],"model":"redwood-embed-1","usage":{}}]}

jess (Support): Thx. Can you also paste response headers from both calls (X-Model-Variant, X-Deployment-Type, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-Request-Id)? That'll help.

alice (Acme Inc.): Hosted headers: X-Model-Variant: redwood-embed-large-1536, X-Deployment-Type: hosted, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 842, X-Request-Id: r-3234
Dedicated headers: X-Model-Variant: redwood-embed-compact-768, X-Deployment-Type: dedicated, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 3, X-Request-Id: d-9981

matt (Eng-ML): interesting — the alias was supposed to map to the same canonical checkpoint across deployments. Looks like Dedicated config has 'redwood-embed-1' pointing to compact 768 model. That explains dims. Not a runtime bug but a mapping/regression.

sam (Eng-Platform): how did that alias change? We push alias updates via model-mapper service. @li can you check the model-mapper config for Acme's dedicated cluster? Also low rate-limit remaining (3) — they're throttled which explains the 429s.

li (Eng-SRE): looking now. grabbing mapping: 
```
# model-mapper:acme-dedicated
redwood-embed-1 -> redwood-embed-compact-768
redwood-embed-1 (hosted) -> redwood-embed-large-1536
```
This was changed by a config patch two days ago (CL: 2025-11-14). Who requested?

matt (Eng-ML): config patch likely intended for a different tenant. We scoped the compact variant for demo clusters but it accidentally had wildcard alias applied to some dedicated tenants. We'll need to revert mapping for acme and check other tenants.

nora (Customer Success): I'll notify Acme that we've identified alias mismatch as the cause. They also reported throughput drop — could that be related?

matt (Eng-ML): alias alone shouldn't change throughput significantly, but compact variant consumes less memory and different batching behavior could change observed throughput. Also the dedicated cluster's rate-limiter config shows much lower burst quota (per-customer override) which explains lower X-RateLimit-Remaining.

sam (Eng-Platform): two parallel actions: 1) revert alias mapping on acme dedicated -> point to redwood-embed-large-1536; 2) increase dedicated rate-limit burst while we investigate. I'll open a patch.

li (Eng-SRE): attempted quick revert in staging, validated responses match hosted (1536 dims). Will schedule controlled rollback to production. ETA 30m.

alice (Acme Inc.): thanks. quick Q: is there a case where batching can truncate or drop dims? they saw one request where embedding array length was < 768.

matt (Eng-ML): truncation to fewer than expected dims is not normal. Could be a serialization bug in private/on-prem nodes for large batches where response buffer gets clipped. But since you saw it only once, suspect partial response due to connection close or proxy chunking. Can you share the raw body + request id (d-xxxxx) for that event?

alice (Acme Inc.): gave raw body for d-9987 (attached). It had an abrupt EOF and payload length header shorter than actual.

li (Eng-SRE): that EOF matches a proxy 502 observed in the node logs at 2025-11-15T03:12:10Z. Looks like an nginx upstream timeout during a large batch (batch_size 128). We're seeing higher p99 latency during peak.

sam (Eng-Platform): ok this reads as: alias mismatch -> wrong model variant causing dimension mismatch. Separately, dedicated cluster had conservative per-tenant rate limits and an occasional upstream timeout for very large batches. Both contributed to the customer's complaints.

jess (Support): plan for remediation?

matt (Eng-ML): 1) revert alias mapping for Acme dedicated to large 1536 model (hotfix). 2) sanity-check model-mapper rules to ensure wildcard rules don't affect tenants — add unit test. 3) inspect and fix proxy timeout for large batch responses; consider increasing upstream buffer and/or chunking. 4) increase Acme's dedicated burst quota temporarily and notify billing if needed.

sam (Eng-Platform): I'm pushing revert now. Deploying model-mapper patch and adding a regression test.

deploy-bot: deployment started: model-mapper/revert-acme-1536 (rollout id mm-457) -> 3 nodes in acme-dedicated.

li (Eng-SRE): rolling restart of the dedicated proxies to pick up new mapping and bump upstream buffers. Will do canary on 1 node then ~10m ramp.

deploy-bot: deployment succeeded on canary node mm-457-canary.

li (Eng-SRE): canary looks good. Dedicated endpoint now returns 1536-d vectors on canary node. No 502s in the 10m window. Proceeding with roll.

deploy-bot: rollout completed mm-457 -> all acme-dedicated nodes.

alice (Acme Inc.): re-tested after 20m. Confirm Hosted and Dedicated now both return 1536-length vectors. Rate-limit remaining increased. Thanks! :tada:

jess (Support): closing the escalation once Acme confirms in prod. We'll follow up with a short postmortem.

matt (Eng-ML): postmortem notes to include: root cause alias wildcard rule applied to tenant; missing unit-test for mapper; proxy upstream buffer/timeout too low for large batch loads; dedicated per-tenant rate-limit defaults too conservative. Action items assigned to eng-ml (matt), eng-platform (sam), eng-sre (li).

nora (Customer Success): I'll send Acme a summary and offer 1 week of elevated burst capacity and a consult on batching config.

jess (Support): For anyone reproducing in future, quick repro checklist we used:
- curl both endpoints (hosted vs dedicated) with same model alias and capture X-Model-Variant + X-Deployment-Type headers
- check embedding array length (len(data[0].embedding))
- if mismatch, query model-mapper: `GET /internal/model-mapper/tenants/{tenant}`
- check rate-limit headers X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Limit
- for truncation/EoF, correlate request-id with proxy logs and look for 502/timeout and `upstream_response_time`
- if large-batch EOF, reduce client batch_size as a temporary workaround (e.g. 128 -> 32)

matt (Eng-ML): extra note: confirm model checkpoint equality by checking model checksum reported in X-Model-Checksum header (we added this last quarter). That guarantees identical weights across deployments.

jess (Support): thanks team. Marking thread as resolved after Acme confirms.

alice (Acme Inc.): confirmed, all good. Appreciate the quick turnaround.
